questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my study destination because of its culture, strong study environment, and the great opportunities to travel and explore other places.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a little difficult to find all the information online before I arrived. However, once I got there, the staff were very helpful and answered my questions, so it was easy to get the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I arrived, I received support from the Erasmus coordinator. They helped me with practical information, answered my questions, and guided me through the arrival process, which made settling in much easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult to find off-campus housing because there is a housing shortage. I would recommend starting the search as early as possible and using the websites recommended by the university, as some of them offer accommodation specifically for Erasmus students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living within the old city walls, as most places are within walking distance and it is a great area to live. It makes it easy to get around and enjoy the city. However, accommodation there can be more expensive than in other areas.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process required checking in through a Zoom meeting. However, the International Office could only assist around 25 students per day, so there were often queues and some waiting time. I would recommend being patient and completing the registration as early as possible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can always get help from the International Office and your Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As long as you follow the instructions on the website, the process is straightforward.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I recommend completing the registration as early as possible to avoid delays.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The overall level of the courses may seem easier than at my home university. However, the exams rely heavily on memorization, so they often require a significant amount of preparation and studying.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was more lecture-based than at UCPH, with less focus on discussions and group work. There was a greater emphasis on independent study and preparing for exams through memorization. Overall, it was a different but valuable learning experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
EU-Institutions and Crisis 
Diplomacy in the XXI Century 
Introduction to Italian Culture 
American Litterature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend these courses:

EU Institutions and Crisis – A relevant course for students interested in European politics and how the EU handles challenges.

Diplomacy in the XXI Century – A good introduction to modern international relations and global cooperation.

Introduction to Italian Culture – A great course for understanding Italian history, society, and culture.

American Literature – Recommended for students interested in literature and cultural perspectives.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend visiting many of the Italian cities around Bologna, as they are easily accessible by train and offer great opportunities to explore different parts of Italy.
